correctness.rationale: Starting from the exact closed homogeneous SIR equations with beta(t)=beta0 exp(at), set Q=beta S/(gamma N), P=beta I/(a N) for a>0. Direct differentiation gives Qdot=aQ(1-P), Pdot=gamma P(Q-1+a/gamma), a genuine predator-prey Lotka-Volterra system. Its first integral H=gamma Q-(gamma-a)log Q+aP-a log P is conserved. For 0<a<gamma, H is strictly convex and coercive in log coordinates; all non-minimal levels are compact regular periodic curves. dI/dt=gamma I(Q-1); the orbit crosses Q=1 exactly twice, generating one strict maximum and minimum each period iff E>H(1,1)=gamma+a. For E<=gamma+a no interior maximum. Incidence logarithmic derivative at the Q turning points is gamma(Q-1), giving at least one strict incidence peak each cycle in the supercritical case. Periodicity of Q,P and exponential beta give exact S,I,C attenuation e^{-aT}. For a<=0, Q strictly decreases; for a>=gamma, P increases, Q has at most one turning point and I at most one maximum. Independent polynomial conservation and exact exemplar (N=gamma=1,a=1/2,beta0=5,S0=2/5,I0=1/10) checked. Finite computations do not establish global periodicity, which follows from compact regular level sets.
residual_risks: The count concerns exact strict maxima of infinitesimally small amplitude at late times.
The infinite-horizon transmission coefficient is unbounded; no empirical claim of repeated observable disease waves.

value.rationale: The coexistence of unbounded transmission growth and indefinitely many *strict* yet geometrically decaying epidemic prevalence/incidence peaks in a closed, non-replenished SIR model is a nonobvious dynamical boundary. It demonstrates that a single log-affine forcing segment can generate unlimited mathematical peak count and provides an exact parameter/energy phase classification, which is useful to distinguish structural peak count from statistical wave-complexity claims. It is not merely an LV relabeling because the original physical observables and attenuation are classified.
residual_risks: Model transmission grows without bound over infinite time; no finite amplitude or observational wave-count conclusion is asserted.

limitations: No practical claim that two interpolation endpoints adequately fit arbitrarily many observed high-amplitude outbreaks.
Peak amplitudes tend to zero; exactly one maximum per period only refers to the nonstationary energy-above-threshold case.
